problem:
The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
v=⟨2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+t⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the vector of the resultant force $F$, in newtons, acting on the particle when $t=1\,\text{s}.$

$F(1)=$
$⟨\,$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$\,⟩\,\text{N}$
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8{t}^{3}-2t,\,\frac{1}{t}+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =6\cdot ⟨8{t}^{3}-2t,\,\frac{1}{t}+1⟩ \\  & =⟨48{t}^{3}-12t,\,\frac{6}{t}+6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $t=1\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1) & =⟨48(1)^{3}-12(1),\,\frac{6}{1}+6⟩ \\  & =⟨36,\,12⟩\,\text{N}.\end{aligned}
$$
